question: Should OpenClaw accept Claws as a core lifecycle owner for globally shared MCP declarations, including authority to register executable stdio commands and share exact declarations across Claws?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow implementation choice: it creates persistent core ownership over a shared, process-facing configuration surface while the RFC and prerequisite stack are still open. Code review cannot decide the permanent trust and ownership model.

options.title: Defer this slice pending RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until maintainers accept or narrow the Claw ownership contract and its prerequisite stack.

options.title: Approve core ownership with explicit safety gates
options.body: Accept the direction only after the PR implements host authorization for sharing, a brokered or allowlisted stdio execution path, and real lifecycle proof.

options.title: Keep MCP ownership outside the Claw core lifecycle
options.body: Route portable MCP capability through an approved bundle or plugin surface instead of adding a second core ownership ledger.

recommendation.title: Defer this slice pending RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until maintainers accept or narrow the Claw ownership contract and its prerequisite stack.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on this PR and their review history covers the lifecycle and schema ownership boundaries that the decision would establish.
